note: P4373 (Pro 30:20) — this is the way of an adulteress: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says 'I have done no wrong.'

dims.v: habitual adultery — sin grown as casual as a meal

the way of the adulteress who eats, wipes her mouth, and says 'I have done no wrong' — habitual sin grown so casual that it is committed and dismissed as easily as a meal, no more troubling to the conscience
the brazen denial that accompanies it (267179)
welded to the seared conscience that denies all wrong

naaph (commit adultery) — 'this is the way of an ADULTERESS'; habitual sin becomes as routine and untroubling as eating. The chilling ease with which she sins and dismisses it shows a conscience wholly seared (cf 5:6; 1 Tim 4:2).
seared conscience — brazen denial of guilt after sin
the saying 'I have done no wrong' after the deed — the brazen, self-acquitting denial of a conscience so seared that it feels no guilt, wiping the mouth as if nothing had happened
welded to the casual adultery it dismisses

aven (wrong/iniquity), denied — 'and says, 'I have done no WRONG''; the deepest horror of habitual sin is not the deed but the untroubled conscience that denies it. Sin becomes invisible to the one hardened in it (cf 30:12; Jer 6:15).
